summary: Every digit can affect an adjacent-pair decision, giving a linear worst-case input-reading lower bound that the single scan already matches, so no genuine principal slower class needs runtime scaling.

optimality.argument: On an all-equal valid string, changing any uninspected digit to a distant value can change the result to false; inspecting all N digits is therefore necessary in the worst case, while the reference checks each of the N - 1 adjacent pairs once.

replacement_checks.evidence: An unread position in an all-equal valid string can be changed to create an adjacent difference greater than two and reverse the required boolean answer.
The accepted reference performs one constant-work comparison for each consecutive pair and retains no input-sized auxiliary structure.

Regression exhaustively checks all 111,100 digit strings of lengths two through five against an independent numeric oracle; authored cases also cover the inclusive threshold, leading zeroes, early and late failures, and maximum length.
